cards.b: Insulin for diabetics, vaccines, cotton that resists bollworm and a tool that can edit a single letter of DNA all come from biotechnology. These tools are powerful and spark debates on safety, ethics and who owns seeds.

In 1973 Herbert Boyer and Stanley Cohen moved a gene from one organism into bacteria. They used restriction enzymes (molecular scissors, found by Arber, Smith and Nathans) to cut DNA, ligase to paste it, and a plasmid as a vehicle.

• PCR (Kary Mullis, 1983): copies a tiny DNA sample millions of times by heating and cooling cycles. Used in COVID-19 RT-PCR tests.
  • Gel electrophoresis: sorts DNA by size.
  • DNA sequencing: Sanger (1977); the Human Genome Project finished in 2003.

Bacteria use CRISPR as an immune memory against viruses. Jennifer Doudna and Emmanuelle Charpentier turned it into a gene-editing tool in 2012 (Nobel 2020).

  1. A guide RNA matches a target DNA stretch.
  2. The Cas9 protein cuts the DNA there.
  3. The cell repairs the cut; scientists can disable or correct a gene.

In 2023 a CRISPR therapy (Casgevy) was approved in the UK and US for sickle cell disease.

Genetically modified crops carry genes from other species. Bt cotton holds a gene from the bacterium Bacillus thuringiensis that makes a protein toxic to bollworm. Golden Rice carries genes to make beta-carotene, a vitamin A source. Concerns include gene flow, pests growing resistant and corporate seed control.

Human insulin by bacteria was marketed in 1982. Dolly the sheep (1996, Ian Wilmut) was cloned from an adult cell. Gene therapy replaces faulty genes. mRNA vaccines use the same idea of instructing cells to make a protein.

The 1975 Asilomar conference set early safety rules. In 2018 He Jiankui announced gene-edited babies in China, widely condemned. Germline editing remains banned or tightly restricted in most countries.

Fix these

  • GM food is not 'DNA that infects you'; DNA is digested like any other.
  • Gene editing is not magic; off-target edits can happen.
  • Cloning does not copy memories or personality.

Khorana's 1970 gene synthesis helped found the field. Bt cotton was approved in India in 2002; it is the only GM crop allowed for commercial cultivation. GM mustard (DMH-11) was cleared by the regulator (GEAC) in 2022 but is under Supreme Court review. India's Department of Biotechnology (1986) and genome-edited rice varieties released by ICAR in 2025 show current work. Biocon and Serum Institute are major producers of insulin and vaccines.

• Recombinant DNA: cut, paste, insert.
  • PCR copies DNA; CRISPR edits it.
  • GM crops like Bt cotton bring benefits and debates.

Think about it:

  1. Should germline editing be allowed to prevent disease? Why or why not?
  2. How can farmers be protected from pest resistance to Bt?
